verdicts.reason: A keeps a sensible headline→copy→CTA left column with the book on the right, but the book has slipped off its backing circle, which floats low on the right; the bottom third is dead space; and the legal line is promoted to near sub-copy size. B puts the CTA above the headline, which breaks the reading order. The CTA's left edge is also out of line with the text column, the book hangs off-centre over a disconnected circle, and the whole lower third is empty.

A has a logical top-to-bottom order (book, headline, copy, CTA) that suits the square format. However, the text block is left-aligned at about x=88 while the CTA is centred, so the two don't share an axis; the circle sits behind the text unrelated to the book; and the margins are uneven. B is the same broken layout as pair 1 B: the CTA sits above the headline with its left edge out of line with the text, the book floats mid-canvas detached from its circle, and the bottom half is empty.
